description: The head of legal for strategic partnerships must approve a co-development and distribution agreement with Northstar Diagnostics and set the agreement's data, economic, export-control, and conflicts terms before signature.

shared_context.S1: The company and Northstar Diagnostics have completed technical diligence for a platform that will support laboratory workflow software and related implementation services.
shared_context.S2: The current draft provides Northstar with distribution rights in North America and includes standard data-use, revenue-share, export, and conflicts language.
shared_context.S3: Northstar wants the agreement signed at the scheduled closing meeting next Thursday.
shared_context.S4: At the final drafting meeting, the firm's ordinary approval process requires the responsible privacy, finance, export-controls, and conflicts lawyers to report any issue that must be reflected before the agreement is signed.
shared_context.S5: Elena Marquez has authority to approve the agreement and its final legal terms.

PF1.text: Owen confirmed during a review of Northstar's proposed data map that the platform will process identifiable patient records as a processor for Northstar; the agreement must prohibit use of those records for model training and require deletion exactly 45 days after termination. He recorded the result in his privacy notes but has not circulated an updated clause.

PF2.text: Maya completed a review of three comparable laboratory-platform deals and confirmed that the appropriate commercial term is an 18% share of Northstar's net receipts, with a quarterly audit right. The benchmark analysis is still in her working file and has not been added to the deal summary.

PF3.text: Thomas verified with the company's export-classification team that the platform's encryption module is controlled technology; the agreement must prohibit access by non-U.S. persons and require Northstar to maintain an export-control compliance program. His confirmation arrived after the standard export language was inserted and has not yet been circulated.

PF4.text: Grace confirmed from the firm's client-matter database that Northstar's parent is an existing client in an unrelated patent matter whose interests could become materially adverse if this alliance fails; execution requires Northstar's informed written consent to the conflict and an ethical screen for the patent-matter team. She has held the confirmation pending the final conflicts review and has not reported it to Elena.

acceptance_conditions: The agreement must not be approved for signature until all required legal controls are reflected or resolved.
Patient-record use for model training must be prohibited.
Patient records must be deleted exactly 45 days after termination.
Northstar's revenue share must be set at exactly 18% of net receipts.
The agreement must include a quarterly audit right.
Non-U.S. persons must be prohibited from accessing the controlled platform technology.
Northstar must be required to maintain an export-control compliance program.
Northstar's informed written consent to the conflict must be obtained.
An ethical screen must be established for the patent-matter team.

decisive_facts.why: The standard data language permits ordinary product use; PF1 changes the agreement to prohibit model training and sets deletion at exactly 45 days after termination.
The draft contains no validated economic benchmark; PF2 changes the revenue share to exactly 18% of net receipts and adds a quarterly audit right.
The standard export clause does not address the classified encryption module; PF3 changes it to prohibit non-U.S.-person access and require an export-control compliance program.
The ordinary conflicts check treats the agreement as executable; PF4 changes execution to require Northstar's informed written consent and an ethical screen for the patent-matter team.
